claims.text: A BFF is a server-side component built for one kind of client: it calls the backend services and returns what that client's screens need, in the shape they need it; one BFF per kind of client lets each client's answers change alone.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 1; glossary backend-for-frontend; ADR 0018 lines 18-20, 26-28

claims.text: Caddy picks a service by path, the same way for every client: every path starting with /api/v1/refunds goes to Payments and every other /api/v1/ path to DonHang.Api. Nothing in the Caddyfile reshapes an API answer; it only chooses where the request goes.
claims.source_hint: Caddyfile @ stage-4 lines 17-32; Caddy docs reverse_proxy, route

claims.text: DonHang.App's calls at stage-4: CatalogApi GET /products and GET /products/$id with no token; OrdersApi GET /orders/$id with signedIn: true and createOrder POST /orders; grep -rnE "_client\.(get|post)\(" DonHang.App/lib/features prints these four lines.

No file under DonHang.App/lib mentions refunds; grep -rn "refunds" Caddyfile DonHang.App/lib prints only Caddyfile lines 24 and 27. So the app never calls Payments and no screen combines the API and Payments.
claims.source_hint: git grep -n refunds stage-4 -- Caddyfile DonHang.App/lib; ADR 0018 lines 12-14

claims.text: fetchOrder sends GET /orders/$id with signedIn: true, throws unless 200, decodes into OrderResult without another service. ApiClient prefixes each path with Caddy's address and /api/v1 and adds the token when signedIn: true, so Caddy sees GET /api/v1/orders/$id.

ADR 0018 decides DonHang.App keeps calling DonHang.Api directly: one kind of client, one team, answers already fit the screens; a BFF solves no current problem while its cost is immediate; Caddyfile and Gateway unchanged.

ADR 0018 names a BFF's costs as one more service to deploy and monitor and one more network hop per request, and rejects an API where clients pick fields because the team must learn, protect and limit load for a new kind of API.

ADR 0018 consequences: no new service; DonHang.Api decides who may read an order, as behind the API gateway; contracts/app/ is checked by api_contract_test.dart and AppContractTests.cs; a future BFF serves only its client, holds no business rules, replaces no service's checks.

ADR 0018 is reopened when a second kind of client (e.g. a shop-staff app) needs answers the API does not fit and changing the API for it would hurt the other client, or when a screen must combine data from the API and Payments.

ADR 0018's feedback section answers 'build a BFF now': inserting a BFF later does not change the API behind it, only the address the app calls; building early pays running cost today for a need not yet present.
Services behind a BFF still check each token themselves, as DonHang.Api and DonHang.Payments already do behind Caddy (each runs AddJwtBearer); a BFF adds no safety.
claims.source_hint: backend.l4.api-gateway summary lines 1-3; DonHang.Api/Program.cs, DonHang.Payments/Program.cs AddJwtBearer @ stage-4

claims.text: A BFF earns its place when clients differ or one screen needs several services combined; without either it only adds a service and a hop. A gateway routes for every client; a BFF shapes answers for one.
Business rules belong in the services, not in a BFF: a rule in one client's BFF does not apply to another client or to a request reaching the service another way.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 6; misconception 3; ADR 0018 line 49-50; backend.l4.api-gateway (defense in depth)

claims.text: A staff app listing orders with refund status meets both reopening conditions, so a staff BFF is worth it; one extra field for the customers' screen goes into the API; a team per client favours a BFF per client owned by that team.
claims.source_hint: What would you choose if… items 1-3; design.l4.conways-law

claims.text: Every DonHang.App request for Đơn Hàng's data lands on DonHang.Api; signing in is the exception, since KeycloakSignIn posts to Keycloak's token endpoint, outside ADR 0018's decision.
